transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lynda Kenyon.
President Trump cast his ballot in Florida today before heading to Georgia to campaign
on behalf of Republican candidates.
Hello to a very special place, Georgia.
Thank you very much, you know.
The president also announced out he is investing $4.2 billion in an automotive plant near
Macon, Georgia.
Former President Obama has been campaigning on behalf of Democrats in Ohio and in Michigan.
People are so ready for something new, so hungry for something better, so sick and tired
of being sick and tired that everywhere you go it feels like change is in the air.
In Michigan, that's what I'm feeling right now.
Obama was speaking in Detroit alongside Abdul El-Sayed, the Democrat running for U.S. Senate.
The former president also blamed Trump administration policies for higher prices.
Clashes erupted in Paris today amid mass protests around the country.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports protests in the city had been largely peaceful through
most of the day.
Members of all ages and backgrounds, students, workers, members of the Yellow Vest movement
coursed down a Paris boulevard.
Many held signs against capitalism and President Emmanuel Macron.
There were chants against the police and for taxing the rich.
Nurse Ginny Bartelamy says things are going downhill in every way.
People are getting so cruel and our children have been beaten up by the police and all
that, so we just say stop.
TV footage showed skirmishes and tear gas in other cities such as Lyon, Marseille, and
Toulouse where protesting was banned.
Eleanor Beardsley in Pierre News, Paris.
Police report nearly 1,000 arrests in France.
The Interior Ministry reported more than 400,000 protesters nationwide.
Remnants of Hurricane Trudy continue moving through the Four Corners region, bringing
with it flooding.
As heavy rains in southern Colorado and northern New Mexico begin to recede, dangerous flooding
conditions remain in Farmington, New Mexico.
Devin Neely is with San Juan County.
The water in both the San Juan and the Animas River is contaminated with raw sewage.
Folks need to stay out of the flood water and there are some severe dangers associated
with the flood waters right now.
Human utilities have shut off power in areas inundated with water.
The National Guard continues to assist with local and state crews with aerial and swift
water rescues in much of northwest New Mexico and the Navajo Nation.
For NPR News, I'm Jami Wanzik in Durango, Colorado.
You're listening to NPR.
Research rockets lifted off over Fairbanks, Alaska this week.
To look at the after-lives of dying stars, Shelby Herbert of Alaska Public Media reports
the NASA experiment is also zooming in on something much smaller, the dust given off
by those stars.
Two rockets pierced thick snow clouds above Alaska.
The first looked at a nebula left behind by a dying star, Messier 27.
The second carried a tiny lab that recreated the extremely hot, gravity-free conditions
inside the nebula that make the tiny grains of dust that make up the universe.
NASA scientist Joe Nooth heads up that project.
If the growth process is efficient, what you make are the equivalent of big rocks.
Nooth says the study could further scientific understanding of the dust produced by volcanic
eruptions and coal-fired power plants, of which Alaska has both.
For NPR News, I'm Shelby Herbert in Fairbanks.
American Express is undergoing some changes.
Despite higher profits in the third quarter, the company is making its first major job
cuts in a decade.
Amex plans to reduce its workforce by 5 percent or about 3,500 employees.
These cuts come amid a 28 percent jump in profits from a year ago or about $3.7 billion
worth of profits.
The CEO of American Express says the layoffs were necessary in order to make the company
more efficient.
I'm Lyndi Kenyon, NPR News, in Washington.

topics.text: Trump votes in Florida, then campaigns in Georgia and announces $4.2 billion automotive plant near Macon
Obama campaigns for Democrats in Detroit, alongside Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, blaming Trump policies for higher prices
Mass protests in France turn violent in Paris and other cities, with nearly 1,000 arrests reported
Remnants of Hurricane Trudy cause dangerous flooding in Farmington, New Mexico and the Four Corners region
NASA research rockets launched over Fairbanks, Alaska to study dust from dying stars
American Express announces first major job cuts in a decade, reducing workforce by about 3,500 despite higher profits
